markdown:
## The Skills Revolution

Google, Apple, IBM, and Delta have all dropped degree requirements for most roles. The results are clear: larger talent pools, more diverse hires, and no decrease in quality.

### The Evidence

| Metric | Degree-Required Postings | Skills-Based Postings |
|---|---|---|
| Applicant pool size | Baseline | +20-30% |
| Diverse applicant rate | Baseline | +18% |
| Quality of hire (1yr review) | 3.8/5 | 3.9/5 |
| Retention (1 year) | 82% | 85% |
| Time-to-fill | 42 days | 38 days |

### Implementation Guide

#### Step 1: Audit Your Requirements

Review every open requisition:

- Is the degree actually necessary for the role?
- Could a non-degreed candidate with the right skills succeed?
- Are you using degree as a proxy for skills you should assess directly?

Rule of thumb : Unless the role legally requires a degree (doctor, lawyer, CPA), it probably does not need one.

#### Step 2: Define Required Skills

Replace "Bachelor's degree required" with specific, assessable skills:

Before : "Bachelor's degree in Computer Science required"

After : "Proficiency in Python and SQL; experience building data pipelines; understanding of software development lifecycle"

Before : "MBA required"

After : "Experience with strategic planning, financial modeling, and cross-functional project leadership"

#### Step 3: Build Skills Assessments

| Assessment Type | Best For | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Work sample test | Technical roles | 2-4 hours |
| Case study | Strategy and analytical roles | 1-2 hours |
| Portfolio review | Creative and design roles | 30-60 min |
| Situational judgment test | Management and customer-facing | 45-60 min |
| Technical interview | Engineering and data | 60-90 min |

#### Step 4: Train Hiring Managers

Many hiring managers default to degree requirements because they are familiar:

- Share data on skills-based hiring outcomes
- Provide alternative assessment methods
- Model the behavior by removing requirements from their own postings
- Celebrate successful non-degreed hires

#### Step 5: Update Systems

- Remove degree fields from screening filters in your ATS
- Add skills tags and assessment scores
- Update interview scorecards to focus on competencies
- Modify offer templates to remove degree verification

### Addressing Concerns

"But how do I know they are qualified?"

Skills assessments predict performance better than degrees. A work sample test has 0.54 validity versus 0.10 for years of education.

"What about foundational knowledge?"

Assess foundational knowledge directly through interviews and tests, not indirectly through credentials.

"Will our clients/partners judge us?"

The world's largest companies (Google, Apple, IBM) have done this. It is becoming the standard, not the exception.

"What about specialized roles?"

For roles requiring licensure (medical, legal, engineering), maintain appropriate requirements. For everything else, assess skills directly.

### Where Skills-Based Hires Come From

| Source | Potential |
|---|---|
| Bootcamp graduates | High (structured training, motivated) |
| Self-taught professionals | High (demonstrated initiative) |
| Career changers | High (transferable skills) |
| Community college | High (practical training) |
| Apprenticeship programs | Very High (learn-by-doing) |
| Military veterans | Very High (leadership + technical skills) |
